options.a: Run each question three times and keep the answer that repeats most often
options.b: Give it the role of an HR director with many years of experience
options.c: Ask it to state how sure it is about each rule that it gives
options.d: Tell it to rely solely on the supplied texts, ignoring its training

explanation.d: Restricting knowledge tells the model to use only the provided documents, not its general knowledge (module 1, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Comparing detects the variation; it does not remove it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A role is a request, not a credential".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A student uses Claude to find sources for an essay and pastes three citations into the bibliography, one of which does not exist. Which two habits would have prevented it? (Select two.)

options.a: Verify every fact that enters graded work
options.b: Use the largest model available, which never invents references
options.c: Tell Claude that the essay is graded, to make it take more care
options.d: Confirm each reference in a library or database
options.e: Ask Claude whether each reference is real before using it

explanation.a: A student checks every fact and citation that goes into graded work, because a hallucination includes "an invented citation, a function that does not exist" (module 9, page 1).
explanation.d: A student checks every fact and citation that goes into graded work, because a hallucination includes "an invented citation, a function that does not exist" (module 9, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because even the documented techniques "don't eliminate them entirely", so no model never invents references.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a plausible-looking fact is a likely continuation whether or not it is true".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A freelance writer uses Claude to draft a short story opening and wants to be sure it is safe to publish under her own name. Which check does the course name for creative work?

options.a: Whether a disclosure line can be skipped for short pieces
options.b: Whether it is too close to an existing piece, and sounds like her
options.c: Whether the plot can be handed to Claude to finish
options.d: Whether Claude's reply says that the opening is original

explanation.b: For creative work the checks are originality, accuracy, tone and whether the piece still sounds like the maker (module 9, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a maker keeps "the idea, the voice, the final choices and the signature".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A team has no benchmark yet and must pick a first model for a mixed set of tasks. What does the models overview advise as the default starting point for most workloads?

options.a: Begin with Claude Haiku 4.5 and move up if it fails
options.b: Begin with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and never test the other tiers against it later
options.c: Begin with Claude Fable 5.1 and move down for cost
options.d: Begin with Opus 5.5, moving to Fable 5.1 if high-effort tests fall short

explanation.d: The overview's default advice is to start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads and use Claude Fable 5.1 when evals at higher effort still fall short (module 3, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The overview's default advice is to start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Having a good evaluation set is the most important step".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the top tier for everything wastes the budget".

quizzes.stem: A designer uses Firefox and a phone, and asks whether Claude in Chrome can be installed there. Which two statements does the course support? (Select two.)

options.a: It is a side panel in a single browser
options.b: It works only on the free plan, which is the one that includes it
options.c: It is a tab inside the Claude web app, so any browser that opens the site has it
options.d: It installs as a desktop extension that runs a local server on the phone
options.e: Other browsers and mobile are excluded

explanation.a: Claude in Chrome is an extension in the Chrome side panel on the paid plans, and "It is not supported on other Chromium browsers or on mobile" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.e: Claude in Chrome is an extension in the Chrome side panel on the paid plans, and "It is not supported on other Chromium browsers or on mobile" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the extension is offered "on the paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Claude in Chrome is a browser extension, in the Chrome side panel", not a page of the web app.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Desktop extensions are for the desktop app only".

quizzes.stem: A start-up needs Claude inside its own mobile screens, with its own conversation storage and tools. Which surface does the page choose?

options.a: Claude Code, the terminal agent for everyday software work
options.b: A Project in the apps, with its own shared files and notes
options.c: Managed agents, hosted and run by the provider
options.d: The Messages API, with the loop and the state written by hand

explanation.d: A product needing Claude inside its own screens uses the Messages API (module 3, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that row is for "A developer wants help changing a codebase".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the apps row reads "Instructions and uploads, not code".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that row is for "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers".

quizzes.stem: A developer team wants a bespoke agent that reuses Claude Code's built-in capabilities, with its own control over orchestration, tool access and permissions. Which surface fits?

options.a: The SDK, which exposes that engine as a library
options.b: Claude Code itself, used as a ready-made tool
options.c: Managed agents, hosted and run by the provider
options.d: The Messages API, called directly with a loop

explanation.a: The Agent SDK lets you build your own agents powered by Claude Code's tools and capabilities, with full control over orchestration, tool access and permissions (module 3, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because that row is for "A developer wants help changing a codebase".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that row is for "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the API row says "Direct access to the model; your own loop, tools and state".

quizzes.stem: A company on a Pro plan wants Claude Tag in its Slack workspace. What does the Tag page say about availability?

options.a: It works on any plan, but only where zero data retention is enabled
options.b: It is for Team and Enterprise subscriptions only, and on Anthropic's own service
options.c: It is offered on every paid plan, including Pro and Max, for any workspace
options.d: It is offered through cloud platforms such as Bedrock as well as directly

explanation.b: Claude Tag is available on Team and Enterprise plans only, on Anthropic's own service, and not for organisations with zero data retention or customer-managed encryption (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because it is "not for organisations with zero data retention or customer-managed encryption, because it stores channel memory and session transcripts".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says it is "available on Team and Enterprise plans only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says it runs "on Anthropic's own service".

quizzes.stem: A free-plan user wants to hand Cowork a folder on her computer. What does the help centre say it needs?

options.a: A terminal with the command-line tool installed
options.b: A Team plan, which is the only plan that has it
options.c: A paid subscription and the desktop app, open and connected
options.d: Nothing beyond a browser with the web app open and a login

explanation.c: Cowork needs a paid plan, and local file access needs the desktop app for macOS or Windows to be open and connected (module 8, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "There is no terminal".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Cowork needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise)".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Local file access, browser use and computer automation need the Claude desktop app for macOS or Windows to be open and connected".

quizzes.stem: A manager asks Claude for a two-sentence reply to a colleague and then for a reusable 40-line status dashboard for her team. Which pair of outputs does the help centre's rule produce?

options.a: The short reply as an artifact and the dashboard inline
options.b: Both as artifacts, opened in a side panel for the manager
options.c: The short answer stays in chat; the larger one opens in a panel
options.d: Both inline, kept in the chat thread as plain text

explanation.c: A short answer stays inline, and significant, self-contained, reusable content becomes an artifact (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because an artifact is made for content "typically over 15 lines, and reusable on its own".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A short answer stays inline in the chat".
explanation.d: Ruled out because artifacts include "documents, code, web pages, images and diagrams, dashboards and interactive tools".

quizzes.stem: A team plans an agent that will update records and send emails by itself. Which approach reflects the course's habit for human and agent teams?

options.a: Treat it as a new colleague: set a scope, review before consequences, keep a log
options.b: Give it full access at first and trim its rights after the first incident occurs
options.c: Let it act freely and read a summary of its work at the end of each month
options.d: Limit it to read-only work and let nobody approve anything that it proposes

explanation.a: The agent is treated like a new colleague with limited access (module 5, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "Start narrow, learn how Claude does on your material, then widen".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the habit needs "a review before consequences".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the questions include "what must a person approve, who is notified of what it did, and where does it stop".

quizzes.stem: An office manager considers letting Claude clear old customer files from a shared drive automatically each night. Which reason from the delegation guidance argues against handing this step over?

options.a: The step tolerates an occasional miss that a reviewer would catch
options.b: A mistake there would be hard to undo once it ran
options.c: The task is small, clear and has a visible result for a person to judge
options.d: The work is shaped like language, so a person must do it

explanation.b: A step stays with a person or code when a mistake would be hard to reverse (module 5, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a good step is "tolerant of an occasional miss that a review will catch".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A small, clear step with a visible result is easier to judge".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a step suits Claude when it is "drafting, summarising, comparing, extracting, rewording, brainstorming".

quizzes.stem: A manager sets a recurring Cowork task for the early morning and wants it to run while her laptop is shut and the desktop app is closed. Which two statements does the page support? (Select two.)

options.a: No awake machine is needed
options.b: Cowork cannot schedule a task at all
options.c: It runs only while the desktop app stays open and connected
options.d: It runs on the laptop and waits until the machine is next powered up
options.e: Anthropic's servers do the job

explanation.a: A recurring task set with /schedule "runs in the cloud, so it does not need your computer awake or the desktop app open" (module 8, page 1).
explanation.e: A recurring task set with /schedule "runs in the cloud, so it does not need your computer awake or the desktop app open" (module 8, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A recurring task, set with a /schedule command".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Tasks run in the cloud on Anthropic's servers", not through the desktop app.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "sessions can continue when your computer is offline".

quizzes.stem: A ceramic artist asks whether to adopt Claude across her practice. Which starting point does the creative-work course recommend?

options.a: Full use from the start, dropped later wherever it harms the style
options.b: Use at every stage of the work, from sketch to final glaze
options.c: Use only for the final signature and the public statements about the piece
options.d: No AI at first, adding it where analysis shows it earns its place

explanation.d: The course recommends a deliberate starting point of no AI, adding it only where analysis says it earns its place (module 9, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the course "recommends a deliberate starting point of no AI".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "audiences, commissioners and platforms may have rules or expectations about AI involvement".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a maker keeps "the idea, the voice, the final choices and the signature".

quizzes.stem: In Anthropic's four-part fluency framework, which official competency matches the course's habit of taking responsibility, and what question does it ask?

options.a: Description: have I said what I want so the job can be done and judged?
options.b: Diligence: will I stand behind this and tell people what Claude did?
options.c: Discernment: is what came back accurate, complete, fair and fit for its reader?
options.d: Delegation: which parts of this job go to Claude and which stay with me?

explanation.b: Diligence is the official name for taking responsibility: will I stand behind this, tell people honestly what Claude did and have I protected the data (module 9, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that question belongs to the habit of describing: "Have I said what I want, so the job can be done and judged?"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table gives that question as "Is what came back accurate, complete, fair and fit for its reader?" for the habit of judging.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that question belongs to deciding what to hand over: "Which parts of this job go to Claude, and which stay with me?"

quizzes.stem: A buyer compares three suppliers' public price pages and fills a quote form, wanting to watch each step. Which tool and approval choice fit?

options.a: Claude in Chrome on trusted sites, each action confirmed, clean profile
options.b: Claude in Chrome with Skip all approvals switched on for speed
options.c: Cowork on the whole drive with Auto approval, letting no single step wait
options.d: Research mode with web search left open on all sites

explanation.a: A step-by-step task on trusted live pages suits Claude in Chrome with manual approval and a clean profile (module 8, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because in that setting "Claude does not pause and nothing checks its actions".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A dedicated folder limits what an injected instruction or a mistake can reach".
explanation.d: Ruled out because Research suits "A job one document answers", and not a step-by-step task that the buyer wants to watch.

quizzes.stem: Six months ago a manager used plain chat for a one-off competitor summary. The work now repeats every week with the same rules and files. What does the course suggest?

options.a: Switch to Claude in Chrome to have the web pages reread each week
options.b: Keep using plain chat for the weekly job as before
options.c: Revisit the choice of tool, moving the routine into a Project or skill
options.d: Move to Cowork and let it run the weekly job on its own

explanation.c: A task that began as a one-off and became weekly deserves a Project or a skill (module 8, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Chrome is for "A step-by-step task on a website you trust".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says to "revisit it when the work changes".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Picking the most powerful surface" is named as a trap.

quizzes.stem: A lecturer asks Claude to draft a marking rubric and then to grade the pupils' essays against it, and records the grades. What stays with the lecturer under the course's guidance?

options.a: Little: Claude can mark and record the essays
options.b: The final signature, once Claude has produced each mark for the class
options.c: The first draft of the rubric, with the grading handed over
options.d: Evaluating the work and any decision that affects the learners

explanation.d: Judging student work and consequential decisions stays with the educator (module 9, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Judging student work and decisions with consequences for a student stay with the educator".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the usage policy treats "academic testing and admissions as a high-risk use needing human review".

quizzes.stem: A team lead tags Claude in a thread to compile a report, then closes Slack for the evening. A colleague adds a correction as a later message. Which two statements describe what happens? (Select two.)

options.a: Replies posted afterwards are followed
options.b: It ignores the late addition, reading only the tagged post
options.c: Work stops once Slack is closed on the lead's device
options.d: It needs a fresh tag before it reads anything new
options.e: The work carries on in the cloud

explanation.a: Tasks run in the cloud, "Claude keeps working after you close Slack", and once in a thread it follows every reply (module 8, page 2).
explanation.e: Tasks run in the cloud, "Claude keeps working after you close Slack", and once in a thread it follows every reply (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because it reads "the thread it was tagged in (including earlier messages when mentioned mid-thread)" and not only the tagged post.
explanation.c: Ruled out because tasks "run in the cloud on Anthropic's servers; sessions can continue when your computer is offline".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a thread it has joined needs no new tag, because "once it is in a thread it follows every reply".

quizzes.stem: A new team member wants Claude to produce the entire quarterly customer review, from data pull to final slides, in one go on day one. What does the delegation guidance suggest?

options.a: Hand over the entire job in one go on day one
options.b: Hand over a small, clear step whose result shows, then widen it
options.c: Hand over only the final slides, with the data pulled
options.d: Hand over everything but ask for a confidence note at the end

explanation.b: Decide how much to hand over at once: a small, clear step with a visible result is easier to judge, so start narrow and widen (module 5, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A good draft does not show the figures were right".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the figures need "Exact numbers, authoritative source" from code or an analyst.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: An operations lead wants to package the team's meeting-notes format so that Claude applies it whenever relevant, and has no programmer available. What is needed?

options.a: A script in Python that calls the API once for each set of notes
options.b: Markdown instructions in the required folder structure, zipped and uploaded
options.c: A connector to the notes folder with write access for the assistant
options.d: A plugin built by a partner company for note-taking and shared with the team

explanation.b: A simple custom skill needs no code: Markdown instructions in the required folder structure, zipped and uploaded (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A simple custom skill needs no code".
explanation.c: Ruled out because skills are "folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically".
explanation.d: Ruled out because partner skills are "From other companies, built to work with their connectors".

quizzes.stem: A team builds a Project knowledge base from a forwarded summary, a draft policy and a thick scan with unreadable pages. Which principle did they ignore?

options.a: Judge the material first, preferring approved primary text
options.b: Remove superseded versions from the knowledge base
options.c: Name an owner and a review date for each file
options.d: Cite the source in each answer given to a reader of the Project

explanation.a: Quality in is quality out: prefer final approved text, primary documents and short clean files (module 7, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Two versions of one document side by side invite Claude to quote either", and the stem lists no duplicates.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "nothing alerts you when a file goes stale", which is about upkeep and not about the quality of what goes in.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a citation shows where an answer came from, not that the source is right".

quizzes.stem: A team wants Claude to use a connector that reads a local application on one employee's machine, not a service on the internet. Which shape fits?

options.a: A skill that bundles the application's instructions for Claude to load
options.b: A custom connector in the directory, which Anthropic has already verified
options.c: A desktop extension, which hosts its endpoint on that same computer
options.d: A remote connector, which reaches an MCP server from Anthropic's cloud

explanation.c: Desktop extensions are for the desktop app only and run a server locally, while remote connectors reach a server from Anthropic's cloud (module 7, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because skills are "folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a custom connector has not been verified by Anthropic".
explanation.d: Ruled out because remote connectors "reach an MCP server from Anthropic's cloud, not from your device".

quizzes.stem: A power user has connected twelve connectors and notices conversations feel crowded with tool lists. Which two statements fit the help centre's suggestion? (Select two.)

options.a: Blocked removes every tool from the list for good
options.b: Needs approval loads each tool only after the user has clicked
options.c: Always allowed keeps the lists short by hiding the prompts
options.d: Load each integration only when the work needs it
options.e: Ten or more is the point where it pays off

explanation.d: The page suggests On demand "when you have ten or more connectors" (module 7, page 3).
explanation.e: The page suggests On demand "when you have ten or more connectors" (module 7, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page describes how "connector tools are loaded", and blocked is a permission instead.
explanation.b: Ruled out because needs approval is a permission, and "require a human click before it writes to it" says nothing about when tools load.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "each tool can be always allowed, needs approval or blocked" is a permission rule, not a loading mode.

quizzes.stem: A team's Project holds a pricing file that nobody has reviewed for a year, and answers drift out of date without any alert. Which practice would have prevented it?

options.a: Telling Claude in the instructions to flag old files whenever it notices them
options.b: Naming an accountable person for each source and fixing a recurring check
options.c: Uploading the file again whenever somebody happens to remember to do it
options.d: Keeping every earlier version in the Project in case it is needed

explanation.b: Each source needs an owner and a review date, because nothing alerts you when a file goes stale (module 7, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "nothing alerts you when a file goes stale".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a stale file should be "a missed appointment, not a surprise".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Old and new documents side by side give Claude two sources to quote".

quizzes.stem: An analyst sets a formatting convention in the Excel add-in's instructions, then finds the Word add-in ignores it. Why?

options.a: Excel instructions work only when macros are enabled in the workbook
options.b: Cross-app work is switched off, which blocks every instruction from passing between apps
options.c: Each one keeps its own rules, so the setting does not carry into another app
options.d: Word needs an Enterprise plan before it can read any instructions

explanation.c: Instructions are set per add-in and do not carry from Excel into Word or PowerPoint (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Macros and VBA, and data tables, are unsupported".
explanation.b: Ruled out because cross-app work concerns files, through "Let Claude work across files".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the add-ins are "installed from Microsoft AppSource, for the paid plans".

quizzes.stem: A paid-plan Project nears its context limit, yet it keeps answering from its large knowledge base. What does the help centre describe, and what follows from it?

options.a: It retrieves the relevant parts, so muddled files spoil replies at scale
options.b: It drops the oldest files one by one until the whole Project fits again
options.c: It folds every file into the instructions and deletes the original files
options.d: It stops accepting questions until enough files have been removed

explanation.a: Near the limit the paid plans switch on retrieval of the relevant parts, and a retrieved passage is only as good as its source (module 7, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because Claude "enables RAG mode, retrieval of the relevant parts" and does not remove files.
explanation.c: Ruled out because retrieval "expands the Project's capacity" and leaves the originals in place.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A big knowledge base is possible" under that mode.

quizzes.stem: A freelancer on a Pro plan asks whether Anthropic uses her chats to improve Claude. What does the course say?

options.a: Only for her incognito chats, which feed improvements to the models
options.b: Only if she opts in through privacy settings, or a conversation is flagged
options.c: Never, whatever settings she has chosen or plan she holds
options.d: Always, with no setting available to stop the use in any plan

explanation.b: Consumer chats are used only if the user allows it in privacy settings, or if a conversation is flagged (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Incognito chats are not used to improve Claude".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "By default Anthropic does not use inputs or outputs from commercial products to train models" applies to Team, Enterprise and the API.
explanation.d: Ruled out because chats are used "only if you choose to allow it in your privacy settings".

quizzes.stem: A user sets Claude in Chrome to its least restrictive approval mode to save clicks while she browses her bank. Which two statements does the page support? (Select two.)

options.a: Claude still reviews each action for safety and blocks anything unsafe
options.b: It is advised for sites she visits often, such as her bank
options.c: It suits only complete trust
options.d: Nothing checks what is done
options.e: Downloads and sensitive entries are still skipped silently there

explanation.c: Skip all approvals means nothing checks the actions, so it is for complete trust only, and the habit is "do not manage financial accounts, legal documents or medical information through it" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.d: Skip all approvals means nothing checks the actions, so it is for complete trust only, and the habit is "do not manage financial accounts, legal documents or medical information through it" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that is the automatic mode, where "Claude keeps working and reviews each action for safety".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the habit is to "prefer Manually approve for anything that matters".
explanation.e: Ruled out because even then "certain things still need your explicit approval".

quizzes.stem: A manager wants to paste an unreleased financial forecast, marked confidential, into a chat tool that the company has sanctioned. Which rule fits?

options.a: Ask Claude to forget the forecast afterwards, which satisfies the rule
options.b: Treat it as internal, so any tool that is approved is fine for everyone
options.c: Treat it as regulated, with no tool ever allowed to receive it
options.d: Permitted there for those who need it, often with identifiers removed

explanation.d: Confidential data goes only in approved tools, with a need to know and often with identifiers removed (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An instruction to forget is not a control".
explanation.b: Ruled out because confidential examples are "Contracts, unreleased financials, customer lists".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the regulated class holds "Health records, payment-card data, government IDs, personal data under GDPR".

quizzes.stem: A security lead wants Claude in chat and Cowork to stop reaching the open web for everyone, without disabling the apps. Which control do the pages describe?

options.a: A lookup-feature switch that account owners set organisation-wide
options.b: A sites allowlist in the browser extension, which also covers chat and Cowork
options.c: A retention setting that deletes browsing history after thirty days
options.d: A per-user prompt telling Claude not to use the internet

explanation.a: Owners can turn web search off for chat and Cowork (module 10, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude in Chrome sites can be allow-listed or blocklisted".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table lists "Retention settings, including custom retention or zero data retention for Enterprise agreements".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A prompt is a request, not a guarantee".

quizzes.stem: An assistant asks a user to confirm "Send this email to everyone on the list?" while she works through a long task, and she presses Allow without a glance. Which two statements does the course support? (Select two.)

options.a: It matters only if the email carries an attachment or a link
options.b: It is a formality that was settled when the task began
options.c: It is harmless: classifiers already screen every action
options.d: Approving unread hands approval to whatever was injected
options.e: The prompt is the control

explanation.d: The confirmation prompt is the control, and the habit is to "read each confirmation before agreeing" (module 10, page 2).
explanation.e: The confirmation prompt is the control, and the habit is to "read each confirmation before agreeing" (module 10, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says to "Use Manual approval for sending, deleting, buying and posting", whatever the email carries.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Do not press Allow out of habit".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the risk is not zero".

quizzes.stem: A team lead tags Claude in a public channel and asks it to summarise what the finance team said in their private channel. What will happen?

options.a: It reads the private room through the tools that an admin connected
options.b: It searches the private room as a person would
options.c: It summarises from a Slack canvas shared in the public room
options.d: It cannot search that conversation

explanation.d: Claude Tag reads other public channels only by searching, and private channels and DMs only from inside them (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Where you tag decides what it can use and who sees the result".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Private channels and DMs are read only from inside them".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A Slack canvas is not readable".

quizzes.stem: A campaign group plans to have Claude send thousands of personal-looking messages to voters that hide their automated origin. Which prohibited category on the policy's list fits?

options.a: Compromising privacy or identity of private persons
options.b: Criminal-justice, censorship and surveillance uses
options.c: Undermining democratic processes, such as deceptive content
options.d: Fraudulent, abusive or predatory practices aimed at customers

explanation.c: The policy lists undermining democratic processes, such as deceptive political content or automated messages that hide their artificial origin (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that category covers "sharing personal information without consent".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that category covers "tracking a person's location without consent or scoring people's trustworthiness".
explanation.d: Ruled out because that category lists "phishing, fake reviews, falsified documents".

quizzes.stem: A consultant sends a client a market summary drafted with Claude, and the client's own policy asks suppliers to say when AI helped. She says nothing. Which responsibility did she skip?

options.a: Data care, such as keeping client files out of the chat
options.b: Accountability for the accuracy of what she sends to the client
options.c: Fairness and impact on the people the summary covers
options.d: Being honest about the tool's part when a rule demands it

explanation.d: Disclosure: be honest about the AI's part when it matters to them, when a policy requires it or when they ask (module 5, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Do not put in what you may not share; anonymise first".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An error in AI-assisted work is your error to correct".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the duty is to "Consider who is affected by the work".

quizzes.stem: A company builds an autonomous agent that acts on customers' behalf, and its lawyer asks whether the Usage Policy's rules apply when no person reads each output. What does the page say?

options.a: Only the high-risk requirements apply
options.b: Unattended operation must still conform, and extra guidance exists for it
options.c: The policy covers chatbots and nothing else, so an agent falls outside its reach
options.d: The rules apply only when a person reads each output before it is used

explanation.b: The policy has universal standards, high-risk requirements and additional guidelines for chatbots, minors, agentic use and MCP servers, and agentic use must still comply (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the policy has "universal usage standards that apply to everyone".
explanation.c: Ruled out because it adds guidelines for "chatbots, products serving minors, agentic use and servers built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP)".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "agentic use must still comply with the policy".

quizzes.stem: A researcher uses Research mode all morning and then finds her usage limits nearly exhausted, though her ordinary chats were few. What explains it?

options.a: Research runs on the free plan, which gives a smaller allowance than paid chat
options.b: Memory was switched on, which re-reads every earlier chat each time it answers
options.c: Research is billed separately, so the ordinary limits are left untouched by it
options.d: It retrieves many sources, which drains allowances faster than simple talk

explanation.d: Research counts against the same limits as ordinary chat but can use them up faster because it retrieves many sources (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Research "needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise)".
explanation.b: Ruled out because memory "holds preferences and context that Claude picked up" and does not re-read old chats.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Research counts against the same limits as ordinary chat".

quizzes.stem: A multi-turn assistant on Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking active fills its window sooner than the team expected, though visible replies are short. What contributes?

options.a: Earlier thinking is stripped each turn, so only the latest turn matters
options.b: Earlier reasoning is retained by default and takes up room
options.c: Visible replies are billed twice, so they fill the space twice over
options.d: Thinking is stored on the server, so it never reaches the request at all

explanation.b: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, and current Opus, Sonnet and Fable models keep earlier thinking by default (module 4, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because current Opus, Sonnet and Fable models "keep them by default".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "each user message and assistant response accumulates in the window", once and not twice.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "It lives in the context".

quizzes.stem: On a Team plan, an analyst's Excel conversation cannot write into the open Word memo, though the add-in works fine in each app. What is the likeliest cause?

options.a: The cross-file setting is off by default there, and set per device
options.b: Excel instructions carry into Word, so the two sets must have conflicted
options.c: Claude can open and switch files itself, so the memo must have been locked
options.d: Word memos can be read by Claude only through a cloud platform

explanation.a: "Let Claude work across files" is off by default for Team and Enterprise, on by default for Pro and Max, and set per device (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because a formatting convention "does not carry into Word or PowerPoint".
explanation.c: Ruled out because it "cannot open, create or switch files itself".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Cross-app work is not supported through Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry or an LLM gateway".

quizzes.stem: A nightly job that summarised last month's reports now fails with a "prompt is too long" error on this month's larger reports, using the same code. Which statement fits?

options.a: Raising the output limit enlarges the window, so the job will then pass
options.b: The request is accepted anyway and simply ends with a stop reason
options.c: The input alone exceeds the window, so it must shrink or the window grow
options.d: A newer tokenizer shrank the text, so the same words now fit more easily

explanation.c: Input that alone exceeds the window is refused with a 400 error on every model (module 1, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Raising it does not enlarge the window".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error" when the input alone exceeds the window.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the same text produces about 30 percent more tokens than on earlier models".

quizzes.stem: A request with thinking active returns an answer cut off mid-sentence, though the output limit was set generously and the input is small. Which two statements explain it? (Select two.)

options.a: The input exceeded the window, which ends the request with an error
options.b: Reasoning tokens count against the same cap
options.c: The model reached a word count that Claude sets for answers
options.d: Less room is left for the visible text
options.e: Thinking text is free, so it leaves the budget alone

explanation.b: Thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens" and leave less room for the visible answer inside max_tokens (module 1, page 1).
explanation.d: Thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens" and leave less room for the visible answer inside max_tokens (module 1, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "max_tokens is a cap on output, not on context".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the loop ends when "the output reaches the max_tokens limit you set", a limit the caller chooses.
explanation.e: Ruled out because the output Claude generates for the turn, "including its extended thinking, counts too".

quizzes.stem: A summarisation job on Claude Opus 5.5 sends short inputs but generates long answers, and the bill is higher than planned. Which price fact points to the lever?

options.a: Output tokens are free once the window is not full, so length is harmless
options.b: Input and output tokens share one price, so only the prompt length matters
options.c: Each produced token costs about five times a fed-in one, so brevity pays most
options.d: A larger window cuts the price of each output token, so a bigger model saves money

explanation.c: The table lists Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, so output costs five times as much and shorter answers save the most (module 3, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the tokens are "billed as output tokens".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the lineup lists "Price per million tokens, input / output".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Larger windows raise the ceiling; they do not remove the need to decide what goes in".
